agent_trace.summary: Subcutaneous air collection on a chest X-ray refers to gas tracking within the soft tissues of the chest wall or neck, often appearing as streaky or mottled lucencies outside the ribs and pleural spaces. In chest imaging, this is distinct from pleural air such as a pneumothorax; similar cases in the training set also involved right apical pleural abnormalities, which can coexist with or be confused for soft-tissue air near the thoracic apex.

key_facts: Subcutaneous air appears as radiolucent streaks or bubbles in the soft tissues of the chest wall, neck, or shoulder girdle.
It lies outside the pleural space and does not conform to lung anatomy or pleural lines.
A chest X-ray can show associated findings such as pneumothorax, pneumomediastinum, or rib/soft-tissue trauma.
Apical and lateral chest wall regions are common places to inspect for soft-tissue air on radiographs.
